propositions: add_comment returns raw ACLI batch envelope with successCount and results markers instead of a normalized comment resource dict, causing type mismatches with consumers expecting {"id": ...} shape
the raw envelope return pattern allows results[].id (a work item key) to be mistaken for a comment id by future consumers reading the result
add_comment skips the normalization idiom used by sibling methods (get_comments, get_issue, create_issue) which parse and verify payloads before returning
the missing id field on Cloud batch envelopes caused _record_comment_id to silently no-op and re-post ~205 comments per hour until hitting Jira's 5000-comment cap

acli_cli_ops._parse_comment_created normalizes the return: resource-shaped dicts pass through verbatim, batch envelopes normalize to {"id": None, "acli_envelope": ...}, unrecognized shapes raise RuntimeError

acli.update_issue also returns raw json.loads passthrough but poses no immediate consumer hazard because _check_mutation_failure guards failure envelopes and the only production consumer treats the return opaquely
